leads.work: Logistics and volume staff keep asking the desk lead (Daren Farmer) to create or extend Sitara deal tickets because gas flowed at a meter with no deal behind it. This happens with small, steady volumes, a day of leftover flow after a deal ends, and a deal that needs rolling into the next month. Then it gets set up in POPS.
leads.why: Many near-identical one-line requests from different people (Aimee Lannou, Ricky Ellis, Mary Poorman, Jackie Young, Karen Lindley) such as 'please extend deal X to cover flow on meter Y'. Some meters come back month after month (989602 in June and again in July; 5593 with the last ticket in July). A rule for automatic roll-over or extension of evergreen deals could remove this.

leads.work: Flow with no matching deal is parked on the HPL Strangers Gas contract. Someone then has to approve writing it off to unaccounted-for gas or create a deal. One unpapered adjustment, made every month for years (TECO Seven Oaks), is cleared by hand.
leads.why: Clem Cernosek sends an approval form covering a year and a half of tiny volumes. Mary Poorman asks about recurring flows on the Strangers agreement (meter 1491, meter 981491). The TECO adjustment has 'occurred each month for the past 5 years' with no paperwork and is hard to reflect in Sitara and Unify.

leads.work: Customer billing disputes about a missing spot deal or a wrong price (CP&L, Conoco, PG&E Texas, LCRA, HL&P). Each one is chased through traders, logistics and settlements by email.
leads.why: The CP&L thread for one $405 difference passed through about 6 people over a week and a later CP&L request followed. Conoco called twice. PG&E sent an invoice for an unknown deal. The LCRA price differed from what was in Sitara. HL&P volumes on 'special days' did not match. Deal entry and confirmation do not line up with what the customer has.

leads.work: Bridge and feedback-monitor errors from POPS, MOPS and Sitara not matching (confirmations on dates the deal doesn't cover) are cleared by hand, often for production months years in the past.
leads.why: Clearing one feedback error for meter 984132 in January 1999 took about 10 emails over 2 weeks among Karen Lindley, Jackie Young, Gary Lamphier, Sherlyn Schumack and Daren. Thomas Engel sends 'keep an eye on the bridge - still erroring out'.

leads.work: Meter allocations and swing rankings in POPS are corrected by hand, along with long-running allocation fixes (CP&L, CILCO, accounting arrangements at meter 692).
leads.why: An allocation error at CP&L was causing part of the UA4 problem. The CILCO issues were described as 'so many CILCO issues' and stayed open for months across several groups. Fred Boas requests contract and rank changes by email.

leads.work: Sitara transport demand charges and deal prices are updated each month to match actual pipeline statements so settlements can redraft invoices (Peoples and North Shore, Enron Canada).
leads.why: Every month there is an Audrey Cook or Kevin Drachenberg request ('update Sitara #131389/#131405 to match the actualized pipeline statements, notify me so I can redraft'), and reminders follow when nothing happens. A pricing mismatch with Enron Canada causes an open OA difference every month now that SAP stops netting it.

leads.work: Each day, origination recognized on desk P&L is reconciled against the origination schedule, and the differences are chased by email.
leads.why: Gabriel Monroy and Binh Pham send nightly emails about unexplained differences ($468, $3,975, $770.68, $11,812). Darron Giron forwards them to others to follow up.

leads.work: Setting up new trading books and portfolios across Tagg, Sitara, Global Counterparty and EOL, plus curve and subregion mapping changes, means passing requests between several groups.
leads.why: Darron forwarded his Tagg book request to show 'how long it took to set it up' (about 2 weeks; it had to go through Global Counterparty and then Ricky Dang). There were separate requests to Imelda Frayre for pipe and curve mapping, to EOL for routing deals by book, and more book requests later.

leads.work: Monthly hours and activity-driver surveys for the transaction costing model are filled out by managers by hand.
leads.why: The survey goes monthly to more than 40 managers. The sender says a standard report could 'eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month'. Path counts are also validated by hand from Unify.

leads.work: Monthly and quarterly explanations of volume variances for Investor Relations (any change over ±10% must be explained).
leads.why: Misti Day: 'It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations', with commercial staff required to verify the numbers.

leads.work: Unfinaled sales and purchase invoices are tracked on spreadsheets sent to department heads each month, with deadlines for the research.
leads.why: Lisa Csikos sends spreadsheets for May production and then for everything before May, saying unfinaled purchases will follow. The work is chased under deadlines set by Sally Beck.

leads.work: Customer nominations arrive by email or Word attachment (Enron Methanol and MTBE, Calpine daily and monthly, Duke Eastrans, Midlothian forecast, Prize Energy revisions, Reliant), along with plant status updates. Schedulers then key them in by hand.
leads.why: The same senders send a nomination every month or every day, often as .doc or .xls attachments. Daren adjusts some by hand (adding 5,000 of swing for Methanol).

leads.work: Pipeline cuts and contract imbalances (Oasis, El Paso, PG&E) are reported in free-text emails, and cut-handling procedures are written out by hand.
leads.why: Mark McCoy sends repeated 'FYI cuts' and imbalance-update emails. Bill Williams sends a cut procedure and asks to be copied on every cut note.

leads.work: Notices of meter shut-ins, outages and pigging are forwarded through long distribution lists, with follow-up letters to producers.
leads.why: Gary Hanks forwards repeated notices (dew point, leaks, McMullen, Baytown pigging rescheduled 3 times, Station 809), each followed by contract checks and producer letters.

leads.work: Weekend on-call notes are written up and handed over by hand, and the on-call person updates POPS and MOPS for each meter.
leads.why: Weekend notes come every weekend and end with 'please check all meters impacted to make sure I Pop'd and Mop'd correctly'.

leads.work: EOL deals have to be checked and controlled by hand: they cannot be changed, failed deals are rebooked by hand, Tagg/Sitara/EOL numbers are cross-linked, and park-and-loan deals are rebooked.
leads.why: Darron lists procedures to follow on 'each and every deal': link Tagg and Sitara, put EOL numbers in Sitara and Tagg, and rebook failures manually. Pat Clynes sends reminders and warnings about EOL deal changes. A park-and-loan EOL deal had to be rebooked as 4 deals and breaks the EOL-to-Sitara reconciliation. A counterparty name was fixed in Tagg.

leads.work: Flash-to-actual reconciliation (fuel on third-party pipes, flashed counterparty volumes that never appear in Unify). Systems also cannot handle fuel charged as part of the price.
leads.why: Fuel was flashed at $83,827 against actuals of $37,662, and a reconciliation effort was asked for. A $1M flash under the wrong counterparty name could not be found. There were monthly July FTA meetings. Sitara can't price fuel, which Steve Venturatos says is 'a nightmare for the Denver office'.

leads.work: Process work when a new EOL product type is set up (hourly peak gas, flexible physical): new GTCs, Sitara handling, comment conventions, and decisions on 24-hour versus hourly positions.
leads.why: Dale Neuner points to 'the myriad of processes involved' in a new product type, with Legal, Sitara and logistics all involved. Workarounds rely on manual comments on tickets.

leads.work: Transport usage tickets are entered and rates updated by hand each month. Buyback tickets for Equistar and Formosa are re-requested whenever a deal expires.
leads.why: Heidi Withers inputs the July tickets and asks for baseload rates. Robert Lloyd needs an Equistar buyback ticket urgently before settlements can close, and asks whether Formosa will have a buyback ticket after its deal expired.

leads.work: The daily Enovate DPR is distributed and approved, with unprotected copies requested by hand, and daily desk P&L is sent by email.
leads.why: There are repeated requests to Daniel Falcone for printable copies, daily 'for your approval' emails, and a corrected EMW P&L email sent after confusion.

leads.work: Old ECT-IM Waha deals keep rolling on evergreen flags and have to be converted to ENA-IM Texas by hand.
leads.why: Thomas Engel says the desk is dead but its deals 'keep rolling'. Daren asks whether they can be changed systematically.

leads.work: PRC and mid-year reviews: collecting accomplishment lists, checking staff rosters, requesting reviewer feedback, and running an all-day committee meeting.
leads.why: Each employee sends a list of accomplishments, managers compile them, HR checks the names, and reviewers are chased for feedback. It happens twice a year.

leads.work: A spreadsheet survey file is passed around by hand: each person detaches, saves, runs it and sends it back. Parking and loan procedures are explained by one-off emails.
leads.why: Darron sends the 'detach, resave, run this file and send it back' instructions to 7 people. Thomas Engel writes out parking procedures, which suggests they are not documented anywhere.

leads.work: Requests to migrate reports and access (CPR Desk Summary report into Sitara reporting; new-hire system access through SRRS).
leads.why: Each person is asked whether the report format is enough. Each new hire needs a list of access requests (CPR, Sitara, Unify).
